suggestions.title: Brand and hero treatment for the landing page
suggestions.what: Give the site a marketing name, a one-line promise and a hero section that leads with the three air-fryer products and what a reader gets (comparisons, buying guides, verified specs). Use Amazon-provided Program Content (images, link formats) served through the link, not scraped screenshots.
suggestions.why: A polished marketing site starts with one clear promise above the fold. Amazon's Operating Agreement makes Program Content (data, images, text, link formats, widgets) available to Associates, so official assets can be used without inventing product photography.

compliance.text: Program Content is made available for advertising items; it excludes product data from non-Amazon sites.

implementation.note: Landing page rebuilt with a hero that leads with the three listings, product cards with the attribute briefs and official listing links, proof stats and an honest status callout. NOT done: the marketing-name decision (Q7) - the site keeps the Zone3 brand; owner picks the name before a rename.
landing page hero rewritten with brand promise and clear CTA; Program Content sourcing rule documented. Compliance basis: S01, S02.

suggestions.title: Editorial article hub built from the verified topic plan
suggestions.what: Publish the 12 working article titles already planned on the Content topics page as real articles: a hub listing them with working titles, the verified Amazon fact each rests on, and a short summary. Give each article a byline, a date and a 'what we verified / what we did not' note.
suggestions.why: Catchy, topic-driven articles are the main organic-traffic lever for an affiliate site, and the topic plan already anchors every title to a fact printed on the listing, so the content has something real to say instead of generic filler.

compliance.text: No topic may state a price, star rating or review count unless Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the API.
No topic may claim search volume, trend direction or conversion data: Amazon publishes no such affiliate endpoint.

implementation.note: Research Desk published at articles/: a hub listing all twelve planned topics with their status and where each lives, plus four full articles written from official pages (two from the ready topics T-09/T-10/T-07, one new evergreen grounded in the Commission Income Statement, one covering T-10's checklist). Every claim carries an inline source link.

suggestions.title: Human-review gate to remove the AI-slop feel
suggestions.what: Before publication, every article passes a review checklist: specific verified specs, no generic filler, no invented experience, the disclosure shown near the recommendation, and a named reviewer. A short 'how this was written' note states which facts were read from which Amazon page.
suggestions.why: The brief asks that the site not read like AI slop. The most defensible way to achieve that without inventing claims is a visible editorial process: every statement traces to an Amazon page, and every article says what was and was not verified.

compliance.text: FTC: you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried.
FTC: the disclosure must be hard to miss and placed close to the recommendation; an 'affiliate link' label or a buy button alone is not an adequate disclosure.

implementation.note: Every article carries a byline (Zone3 Research Desk), a date, a reading time, a 'what we verified / what we did not verify' box, a 'how this was written' note naming the pages read, and its editorial constraints. The review checklist is published on the hub. No first-person product experience appears anywhere.

suggestions.title: Comparison and buying-guide pages in marketing style

suggestions.why: Comparisons and buying guides are the highest-intent content for air fryer buyers and convert readers into clicks; a clean matrix plus a decision guide reads like a real marketing site rather than a data dump.

compliance.text: Prices, availability, ratings and review counts may appear only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API.

Logged in COORDINATION.md as a change request rather than edited cross-scope. comparison matrix restyled with who-this-is-for buying guide; only verified attributes shown; blanks retained for price/rating/review/commission per S02 2(b)/6(t).

suggestions.what: Add a trust section explaining the verification protocol: every value comes from an official Amazon or FTC page, unverified cells stay blank, and the Flagged for review page publishes open items with their source links.
suggestions.why: Affiliate trust is a conversion factor. The site already has a verification discipline; presenting it plainly distinguishes it from sloppy AI sites and answers the credibility question before a reader clicks.

suggestions.why: The brief asks for trendy topics. A trend claim with no source is exactly the AI-slop the brief wants avoided; anchoring to a named, dated official surface keeps the section honest and still feels current.

No search-volume or trend-direction claims may be made.

suggestions.why: The brief requires click/conversion tracking and continuous optimization. Amazon's own reporting is the compliant data path; it also feeds the ledger with values that can be sourced rather than guessed.

questions.question: What is the Associates tag (tracking ID) to use on every Special Link?
questions.what_we_know: Every Special Link must carry the Associates tag; without it no link on the site is trackable for commissions.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The tag value. No document read in this project contains it.
questions.why_it_matters: Blocks SUG-05 (CTAs) and every commission-earning link on the site.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner supplies the tag from Associates Central. Record it in the coordination log; do not store it in public files.

questions.question: Are the three destination listings the products that were intended?
questions.what_we_know: Each submitted short link opens a specific live listing: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH. The mapping is stable across captures by three sessions, but no official source ties the links to the intended products.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's intent behind the three submitted links.
questions.why_it_matters: All product content, comparisons and buying guides depend on identity. Wrong identity means the site promotes products the owner did not choose.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner confirms the three intended ASINs. If the intended products differ, re-run the intake and re-verify before any content is published.

questions.question: Which Amazon marketplace is the site for?
questions.what_we_know: Operating Agreement Schedule 1 lists one location for this agreement text: United States, amazon.com. Commission tables are per-locale.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner wants to target other locales or stay US-only.
questions.why_it_matters: Links, rates and eligible products differ per marketplace; the site's current data is US-only.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. If other locales are wanted, each needs its own verified commission table and link set before content is written.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled, and does it meet the Creators API prerequisites?
questions.what_we_know: The Creators API requires enrolment and at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days; the application review requires three qualifying sales in 180 days and excludes personal orders.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The account's enrolment status and sales history.
questions.why_it_matters: Price, availability, ratings and review counts can only appear on the site when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API. Without API access those cells stay blank.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner checks Associates Central. Record the result; the site's blank cells are the fallback until then.

questions.question: Who reviews and publishes content, and at what cadence?
questions.what_we_know: The site already publishes a verification protocol and a flagged-for-review process.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's cadence and named reviewer.
questions.why_it_matters: The human-review gate (SUG-03) is the main defence against the AI-slop feel; without a real reviewer it is cosmetic.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner assigns a reviewer and a cadence; record the decision before scaling the article hub.

questions.question: Will the products be used or tested first-hand?
questions.what_we_know: FTC guidance states you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner will purchase or test the three products.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether first-person 'we tested' style content is allowed. Without first-hand use, all content must stay attribute-and-fact based.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. If no testing, the editorial rule stays: only verified listing facts and official document facts.

questions.question: What brand direction (name, palette, voice) should the marketing site use?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing official restricts the site's own brand; the only mandated text is the Associates disclosure.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's preferred name, colors and tone.
questions.why_it_matters: Drives the polished-marketing look (SUG-01) and all page styling.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner picks from options or supplies brand assets; record the choice in the coordination log before implementation.

questions.question: Which analytics and reporting stack will be used for clicks and conversions?
questions.what_we_know: Amazon's own reports are the compliant source for clicks and conversions, and the participation requirements prohibit artificially generated clicks or sessions. The site-side half of the question was built on 2026-11-17: five defined events, a privacy-preserving outbound-click counter on every published page, and a tested self-hosted collector.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Where the collector runs, and whether the owner accepts the proposed event set. Nothing has been collected yet, so the site still has no traffic evidence.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines how the Campaigns ledger gets real values and how optimization is measured.
questions.how_to_discover: One owner step: set one endpoint in data/analytics/config.json. Until then the counter keeps its events in the reader's own browser and sends nothing.

questions.question: What budget and tooling exist for keyword and topic research?
questions.what_we_know: Amazon publishes no affiliate search-volume, keyword-difficulty or conversion-rate data, so no such claim can be made on the site.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's budget and preferred tools.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines how article priority is decided; external keyword tools can suggest topics but their numbers must never be presented as Amazon facts.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner supplies budget/tools; record which tools are approved before use.

questions.question: Should the disclosure placement be reviewed by counsel before launch?
questions.what_we_know: The required wording is fixed by the Operating Agreement; FTC guidance requires the disclosure to be clear, conspicuous and close to the recommendation.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner wants a formal legal review.
questions.why_it_matters: Disclosure breaches are treated as a material breach of the agreement; placement decisions carry compliance weight.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision; if yes, review the disclosure pattern on every page template before publishing.

questions.question: Do the two unregistered product links belong in the project at all — and what products do they stand for?
questions.what_we_know: The 2026-11-17 owner brief lists five link.amazon short links. data/products.json registered only three of them (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, re-checked as S67-S69); a repo-wide search on 2026-11-17 found no register row, observation or flag for B0c8moW59 or B0f3GKalj before this session added the two 'not registered' rows to the intent record.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the two links are live, what product each is meant to point at, and whether the owner still wants them promoted.
questions.why_it_matters: A shop page cannot sell a product whose identity is unrecorded; the comparison, the chooser and every CTA would silently cover three links while the brief promised five.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner confirms each of the two links in the enrolled Associates workflow (or withdraws it). Flag G82-F-03 tracks the gap; the new rows in the Product-intent confirmation record on products.html are where the answers land.

questions.question: Which reader layer becomes the canonical shop the owner shows buyers — site/, read/, or marketing/?
questions.what_we_know: Three reader-facing layers now cover the same three products with overlapping topics (the guide register's own duplication note and flag Z14-F-04 say so). The brief asks for 'one site to index'. Nothing in the repo records an owner choice.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Which brand voice wins (Air Fryer Field Notes vs The Crisp Report), and what happens to the losing layers (cross-link, archive or merge).
questions.why_it_matters: Near-duplicate pages across three layers are the strongest 'generated' tell left on the site, and they split any future organic traffic between them.
questions.how_to_discover: Answering this selects design path DP-C in the review below. No further data needed — it is a choice, not a fact to verify.

workflow: 1. Review this page with the suggestions (SUG-01 to SUG-10) and the open questions (Q1 to Q10) side by side.

paths.name: Shopfront first, lab underneath
paths.thesis: A buyer decides in seconds at the shelf; the verification machinery stays one click away but never above the fold. The site stops reading like an audit by changing what is FIRST, not by adding decoration.
steps: Open site/index.html with the three-question chooser already built for this purpose (decision D-23 in the brief's list) — move it above the product cards; every answer deep-links to the comparison row it affects.

Give each product card a 'fits you if / not for you if' pair of lines generated ONLY from quoted listing features — the generator already blocks any other sentence (i2_gate G6/G7), so catchiness comes from layout, not from invented claims.
Below the cards, one strip: 'New this week from the guides desk' fed by the same register that now backs feed.xml; dated, never ranked.
Disclosure strip stays exactly where it is (above the fold, every page, repeated in the footer) — the polish must not move it, and the lint enforces that it wasn't.
Keep every dashboard surface (flagged, sources, verification, decision pages) reachable from the footer and the single nav group — already true; do not add nav items, fold new ones in.
paths.resolves: The look half of SUG-01 and SUG-04; the brief's 'lead with the products' rule; consistent with S-17/S-19 as implemented.
paths.effort: One generator pass over site/ home + front-door region; no new data files; every gate already exists.
paths.risk: Low. Worst case the page reverts on a rebuild — the same self-healing pattern the feed uses now covers it.
paths.do_not: No prices, no star ratings, no review counts, no 'bestseller' badge until the API feed exists (2(b)/6(t)); no 'trending' without a dated first-party snapshot (the evidence rule already adopted).

paths.name: Magazine desk: voice and cadence carry it
paths.thesis: The fastest way to stop reading like AI slop is a real editorial calendar with a named human gate: one dated question per week, an author byline, and a 'what changed since last read' box that only a desk that re-reads sources can write.
steps: Adopt the cadence in the review below: one guide per week, each new guide lands in sitemap + feed automatically because both are register-driven now.

Add a byline block ('Field Notes desk — reviewed by: <name>') once Q5 names the human reviewer; until then the reviewed_by line stating 'no human editor' stays (it is already there; polishing would mean removing it, which we will not do).
Two held topics become publishable ONLY with owner inputs: testing/first-hand use (Q6) or the API for figures (Q4); do not write them softer to ship them.
Keep titles question-shaped like the five live guides; the brief's own suggested titles are all published — the next topic should come from the D8 query report, not from instinct.
paths.resolves: SUG-02, SUG-03, SUG-10, S-07's cadence half, and the 'catchy trendy articles' ask — honestly: catchy within what the compliance gates allow.
paths.effort: Editorial continuity, not code: the machinery (register, lint, feed, sitemap) already carries a weekly page in under an hour.
paths.risk: Cadence decays without a named owner; the site must never ship a 'latest' widget that goes stale — the register dates everything for exactly this reason.
paths.do_not: No synthetic social proof, no 'most popular', no AI-author persona names.

paths.name: Consolidate, then decorate
paths.thesis: Three parallel reader layers (site/, read/, marketing/) say near-the-same things about the same three products in three voices. That is both the strongest 'generated' tell and the reason search cannot pick a winner. One canonical layer fixes the findability ask and most of the slop feel at once.
steps: Owner answers Q12 (choose the canonical layer). Recommendation recorded here: promote site/ (the layer with the working house lint and release gates) and mark read/ + marketing/ as companion research with cross-links, not duplicates.
One navigation, one feed (the new feed.xml grows to cover the layer chosen), one sitemap (already covers everything; consolidation is a link-and-banner change, not a build change).
Fold the surviving extras (photography once S-18 decides, any API data once Q4 clears) into the chosen layer only, so polish is not written three times.
paths.resolves: 'One site to index and a reason to rank it' from the brief; Z14-F-04; the duplication note; most of Q7's brand-open residue.
paths.effort: Small edits, but touches the most shared files in the repo — must be ONE integration session (per the coordination protocol), not three parallel ones.
paths.risk: Link churn: internal cross-links and the sitemap shift. The gates in scripts/ catch every broken one before push.
paths.do_not: Do not delete the losing layers (history rule: archives stay); do not hand-merge the three feeds of copy into one without re-running every gate on the result.

paths.name: Measure first, then write (the owner's brief, built)
paths.thesis: The brief's instruction is to turn on click and conversion measurement before writing anything else. That half is now built and published; the remaining half is an owner step, not a build step.
steps: Set one endpoint in data/analytics/config.json; the collector is in tools/collector/ with both hosting options documented.
Accept or amend the five events in DEC-03; the client is generated from the register, so an amendment is one line plus a rebuild.
Connect Search Console (discovery action D8) so the query side of the next-topic decision has measured input.
Then choose the next guide topic from measured arrivals, not from instinct.
paths.resolves: The measurement half of SUG-09 and the 'measure whether anyone arrives' half of the publishing cadence.
paths.effort: One owner step and one rebuild.
paths.risk: Low. Until the endpoint is set nothing changes about what the site does.
paths.do_not: Do not add an identifier to reach unique-visitor counts without a consent decision (G3c-F-05). Do not publish an event count as a traffic, popularity or earnings figure.

review_2026_11_17.cadence: Proposed cadence (owner-adoptable, changes nothing until accepted): one guide per week from the register's held queue as soon as its blocker clears; each ship = register row + rebuild + gate run (all mechanical). Measure with D8; the ledger rule stands: timestamp, source, channel, eligible sessions, clicks and orders ONLY from authorized first-party reports, kept dated, no forecast. Until Search Console data exists, the next topic after the held queue is chosen by the brief's own question list, not by claimed search volume.

restatus.change: Owner brief of 2026-11-17 names the selected tracking ID; per Q1's own rule the value is recorded in the coordination log (COORDINATION.md, Part 82), not repeated on public pages. It cannot be verified from inside this repo (account-side), and the brief's workflow says to test ONE Special Link before scaling links; until that test is recorded, the site keeps evidence-mode links.
The intent record on products.html is the place the answer goes, one column-set per link; three of five links keep dated redirect observations (S67-S69) that remain separate from intent by rule.
All recorded destinations are amazon.com; the owner's profile is SG. Nothing in the repo decides this; a .sg decision changes link targets, disclosure review and copy language together.
Gates the held 'best value' guide, every figure, and the SUG-05 CTA. Owner-side; no repo action possible.
Cadence proposal + machinery (register-driven feed/sitemap) shipped this pass; the human reviewer is still unnamed, and pages say so honestly in the meantime.
S-06 stays 'not adopted' per the recorded decision; guides keep their 'no invented experience' rule and it is enforced, not aspirational.
site/ carries the 'Air Fryer Field Notes' brand + style guide + logo tile; the brand name is recorded as chosen in the brief (S-15). What is NOT decided is which layer owns the brand — see Q12/DP-C.

The stack is no longer undecided: the site measures with its own first-party counter (five defined events, no cookie, no identifier, no third party) and the collector it posts to is built and tested in tools/collector/. What is left is one owner step - the host - and the acceptance of the event set. The search half of the question (Search Console) is unchanged and still open.
The brief lists no budget; the D8 query report is the free path, and the cadence section is written so it works on free inputs alone.
No answer arrived; the shipped default (disclosure above the fold on every page + footer repeat + banner link) already meets the letter of S01 §5 and the FTC guidance cited in the register.
Two of the brief's five links have no register row; see flag G82-F-03 and the two 'not registered' rows in the intent record.
Which reader layer is canonical. The answer selects DP-C and settles the last brand question.

how_to_choose: Use the Accept/Reject/Defer control on the review console (decision-queue.html) or the decision tools on site/decisions.html; either export becomes the record a later session implements from.
The paths are ordered: C decides the surface, A decorates it, B runs it. A is compatible with B on any layer choice; C is a prerequisite for 'one site to index', not a style opinion.
Nothing above is implemented by accepting it; an unblocked path (C's banners, A's copy) is one gate-green build away once a decision is recorded.
Blocked items stay blocked visibly (Q4-family): the site would rather show a gap than fill it with a guess — that IS the trust design.
